title: Norman Conquest
summary: Duke William's claim to the English throne — told through the battles of a single fateful year that replaced Anglo-Saxon rule with a Norman dynasty.

stories.summary: Three battles, two kings dead, and a new ruler crowned in Westminster.

events.title: Stamford Bridge
events.body: King Harold Godwinson marched north at speed and surprised an invading Norwegian army led by Harald Hardrada at Stamford Bridge. The English victory was total — but it left Harold's forces exhausted just as William's fleet was crossing the Channel.

events.title: Norman Landing at Pevensey
events.body: William, Duke of Normandy, landed unopposed at Pevensey on the Sussex coast while Harold was still in the north. His army fortified a camp and began ravaging the countryside to lure the English king into battle on ground of William's choosing.

events.title: Battle of Hastings
events.body: Harold rushed south and confronted William near Hastings. All day the Norman cavalry charged the English shield wall on Senlac Hill; late in the afternoon Harold was killed — tradition says by an arrow in the eye — and the English line collapsed.

events.title: March on London
events.body: After Hastings, William advanced cautiously toward London, burning and fortifying as he went. English resistance crumbled as nobles submitted; the city opened its gates and William entered Westminster to claim the throne Edward had once promised him.

events.title: Coronation of William
events.body: William was crowned King of England in Westminster Abbey on Christmas Day. When Norman guards outside mistook the cheering inside for a riot and set fires, the new king trembled on his throne — an omen, some said, of the violent years ahead.

stories.title: The Harrying of the North
stories.summary: William's brutal suppression of northern rebellion.
